nodes.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite multi-stack Turing machines with label sets $\Lambda_1$ and $\Lambda_2$, and let $X$ be the alphabet of the input stack of $M_2$. The label set of their composite machine is the disjoint union of $\Lambda_1$, $\Lambda_2$ and two copies of $X \sqcup \{\bot\}$, one for each copy loop: in each copy, $\bot$ labels the step that pops and $x \in X$ labels the step that pushes $x$.
nodes.title: Labels of the composite machine

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite multi-stack Turing machines with internal state sets $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$, and let $X$ be the alphabet of the input stack of $M_2$. The internal states of their composite machine are the triples in $\sigma_1 \times \sigma_2 \times (X \sqcup \{\bot\})$: a state of $M_1$, a state of $M_2$, and either the symbol just popped by a copy loop or $\bot$ when there is none.
nodes.title: States of the composite machine

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite multi-stack Turing machines and let $X$ be the alphabet of the input stack of $M_2$. The stacks of their composite machine are the stacks of $M_1$, the stacks of $M_2$ and one scratch stack. Each stack of $M_1$ keeps its alphabet from $M_1$, each stack of $M_2$ keeps its alphabet from $M_2$, and the scratch stack has alphabet $X$.
nodes.title: Stack alphabets of the composite machine

nodes.summary: For finite multi-stack Turing machines $M_1$ and $M_2$ with stack index sets $K_1$ and $K_2$, the stacks of their composite machine are indexed by the disjoint union $K_1 \sqcup K_2 \sqcup \{\ast\}$: the stacks of $M_1$, the stacks of $M_2$, and one scratch stack $\ast$.
nodes.title: Stack indices of the composite machine

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ be types with canonical bitstring encodings. If $f : \alpha \to \beta$ and $g : \beta \to \gamma$ are polynomial-time computable, then so is $g \circ f$.
nodes.title: Polynomial-time functions are closed under composition

nodes.summary: Let $h_1$ be a polynomial-time TM2 computation of $f : \alpha \to \beta$ with respect to encodings $e_\alpha$ and $e_\beta$, and let $h_2$ be one of $g : \beta \to \gamma$ with respect to $e_\beta$ and $e_\gamma$. This is the polynomial-time TM2 computation of $g \circ f$ with respect to $e_\alpha$ and $e_\gamma$ whose machine is the composite machine of the machines of $h_1$ and $h_2$ with the glue map between…
nodes.title: The composite polynomial-time TM2 computation

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a decision problem on bitstrings and let $f$ be a polynomial-time computable function from bitstrings to bitstrings. If $L$ is in P, then $L \circ f$ is in P. In particular P is closed under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
nodes.title: P is closed under polynomial-time preimages

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$ compute $f : \alpha \to \beta$ in polynomial time from the encoding $e_\alpha$ to $e_\beta$, and let $M_2$ compute $g : \beta \to \gamma$ in polynomial time from $e_\beta$ to $e_\gamma$. For every $a \in \alpha$, let $n$ be the length of $e_\alpha(a)$ and $T$ the composite time bound. Started on $e_\alpha(a)$, written in the input alphabet of $M_1$, the composite machine of $M_1$ and $M_2$ (with the glue…
nodes.title: The composite machine computes the composite function in time

nodes.summary: Let $p_1, p_2 \in \mathbb{N}[X]$ be the polynomial time bounds of a machine $M_1$ computing $f$ and a machine $M_2$ computing $g$, and let $c$ be the sum, over the labels of $M_1$, of the number of push instructions in the statement at that label. The composite time bound is the polynomial $p_1 + 4(X + c\,p_1) + 2 + p_2 \circ (X + c\,p_1)$.
nodes.title: Time bound of the composite machine

nodes.summary: Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ be finite multi-stack Turing machines, let $X$ be the alphabet of the input stack of $M_2$, and let $\varphi$ map the output alphabet of $M_1$ to $X$. The composite machine has the stacks of $M_1$, the stacks of $M_2$ and one scratch stack with alphabet $X$; its input stack is that of $M_1$ and its output stack is that of $M_2$. It starts at the main label of $M_1$, in the state made of the…

nodes.summary: For every polynomial $p$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{N}$ and all natural numbers $a \le b$, we have $p(a) \le p(b)$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of a natural-number polynomial is monotone

nodes.summary: Let $h_1$ be a polynomial-time TM2 computation of $f : \alpha \to \beta$ and $h_2$ one of $g : \beta \to \gamma$, where $\beta$ is encoded by lists over an alphabet $\Gamma_\beta$. A symbol $y$ of the output-stack alphabet of $h_1$'s machine is sent to the symbol of the input-stack alphabet of $h_2$'s machine that corresponds, under $h_2$'s input alphabet bijection with $\Gamma_\beta$, to the letter that $y$…
nodes.title: Symbol translation between composed machines

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite multi-stack Turing machine (Mathlib's TM2 model with finitely many stacks, function labels and internal states, and a finite input alphabet) with input stack $k_0$, and let $l$ be a list of symbols from the alphabet of stack $k_0$. Then for every stack $k$ of $M$, the stack $k$ in the initial configuration of $M$ on input $l$ has length at most the length of $l$.
nodes.title: Stacks of the initial configuration are no longer than the input

nodes.summary: Let $f : \alpha \to \mathrm{Option}\,\alpha$ and $g : \beta \to \mathrm{Option}\,\beta$ be partial step functions (a value $\mathrm{none}$ means halting) and $e : \alpha \to \beta$ a map such that $f(c) = c'$ implies $g(e(c)) = e(c')$ for all $c, c'$. Then for every $n$ and all $c, d \in \alpha$, if $n$ steps of $f$ starting from $c$ end at $d$, then $n$ steps of $g$ starting from $e(c)$ end at $e(d)$.
nodes.title: Simulation transports runs

nodes.summary: A label $l$ of $M_1$ is sent to $l$ viewed as a label of the $M_1$ part of the composite of $M_1$ and $M_2$, and the halted label is sent to the label that pops $M_1$'s output stack, which starts the first copy loop.

nodes.summary: Let $h_1$ be a polynomial-time TM2 computation of $f : \alpha \to \beta$ with polynomial time bound $p_1 \in \mathbb{N}[X]$, and let $c$ be the push bound of the machine of $h_1$. This is the polynomial $X + c\,p_1 \in \mathbb{N}[X]$.
nodes.title: Intermediate length bound of the composite machine

nodes.summary: Given finite multi-stack Turing machines $M_1$ and $M_2$, contents $S_1$ for the stacks of $M_1$, contents $S_2$ for the stacks of $M_2$, and a list $t$ of symbols of $M_2$'s input alphabet, the stack contents of their composite machine put $S_1(k)$ on the copy of each stack $k$ of $M_1$, $S_2(k)$ on the copy of each stack $k$ of $M_2$, and $t$ on the scratch stack.
nodes.title: Assembling the stacks of the composite machine

nodes.summary: In the composite machine of $M_1$ and $M_2$, this is the label $\mathrm{none}$ in the first copy-loop part of the label set; the composite program uses it to pop a symbol from $M_1$'s output stack.
nodes.title: Pop label of the first copy loop

nodes.summary: In the composite machine of $M_1$ and $M_2$, this is the label $\mathrm{none}$ in the second copy-loop part of the label set; the composite program uses it to pop a symbol from the scratch stack.
nodes.title: Pop label of the second copy loop

At a label of $M_1$ or of $M_2$ the composite program runs the lifted statement of that machine at that label. nodes.summary: For a finite multi-stack Turing machine $M$ (Mathlib's TM2 model with finitely many labels), the push bound of $M$ is the sum, over all labels $l$ of $M$, of the number of push instructions in the statement that $M$ assigns to $l$.
nodes.title: Push bound of a finite multi-stack Turing machine

nodes.summary: In the composite machine of $M_1$ and $M_2$, for a symbol $x$ of $M_2$'s input alphabet, this is the label $\mathrm{some}\ x$ in the first copy-loop part of the label set; the composite program uses it to push $x$ on the scratch stack.
nodes.title: Push labels of the first copy loop

nodes.summary: In the composite machine of $M_1$ and $M_2$, for a symbol $x$ of $M_2$'s input alphabet, this is the label $\mathrm{some}\ x$ in the second copy-loop part of the label set; the composite program uses it to push $x$ on $M_2$'s input stack.
nodes.title: Push labels of the second copy loop

nodes.summary: For a statement $q$ of a multi-stack Turing machine (Mathlib's TM2 model), this is the number of push nodes in $q$: a push node counts $1$ plus the count of its continuation; peek, pop and load nodes count as their continuation; a branch counts the sum of its two branches; goto and halt count $0$.
nodes.title: Number of push instructions in a TM2 statement

nodes.title: Polynomial-time TM2-computable functions are closed under composition

nodes.summary: For multi-stack Turing machines (TM2 machines) $M_1$ and $M_2$ with stack index types $K_1$ and $K_2$, the composite machine has stack indices $K_1 \oplus K_2 \oplus \mathrm{Unit}$; its scratch stack is the index given by the unique element of the $\mathrm{Unit}$ summand.
nodes.title: Scratch stack of the composite machine

Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
